title: Generic Distinguisher for Three-Round Substitution-Permutation Networks
summary: The three-round yoyo structure preserves a zero-difference pattern, but its external recognition remains unresolved; determine whether the relation has a generic distinguishing property and construct a distinguisher if it does.

formal_statement.body: For a generic three-round substitution--permutation network with substitution layer $S$, let $U$ and $V$ be complementary linear subspaces of the ambient vector space, and consider $x,y\in U$ and $z\in V$ such that the ciphertext difference satisfies $c_1-c_2=S(x+z)-S(y+z)$. Determine whether this relation has a recognizable generic distinguishing property and, if so, construct a generic distinguisher. Such a distinguisher would also apply to the analogous plaintext relation using $S^{-1}$ and corresponding complementary subspaces $U'$ and $V'$.

scope.domain: Structural and differential cryptanalysis of generic three-round substitution-permutation networks and yoyo-induced difference relations.
assumptions: U and V are complementary linear subspaces of the ambient vector space
x and y belong to U, while z belongs to V
parameters: U and V: subspaces defining the ciphertext-side relation
x, y, and z: elements defining the structured difference
S inverse, U prime, and V prime: the inverse substitution and corresponding plaintext-side analogue
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the specified ciphertext-difference relation has a recognizable generic distinguishing property and, if so, construct a generic distinguisher; the same distinguisher would apply to the analogous plaintext relation using the inverse substitution and corresponding subspaces.

progress.summary: The source presents this as a problem for further study after its three-round yoyo analysis identifies a preserved zero-difference pattern that the adversary cannot externally recognize. It asks whether the resulting ciphertext relation has generic distinguishing properties and whether a distinguisher can be constructed, with an analogous plaintext application.
citation_labels: Sondre Rønjom et al., Yoyo Tricks with AES
